summary: WorldEntity duplicate-ID diagnostics do not satisfy the documented both-origins contract: the diagnostic keeps kinds and recipe keys but drops worldId, regionId, generator, and generatorVersion, so materially different competing origins can become diagnostically indistinguishable. Recommend a bounded source/test follow-up after the active WorldEntity completion train rather than widening PR #293.
evidence: Docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states that the domain registry rejects duplicate live IDs, keeps the first registration authoritative, and emits a diagnostic describing both origins.
At active PR #293 exact head 91b6e273c0c21326dfbfe9c5ee5227e99f26933e, DuplicateIdentityDiagnostic contains entityId, existingKind, incomingKind, existingRecipeKey, and incomingRecipeKey only.

Registry duplicate construction copies only existing.origin.recipeKey and incoming origin.recipeKey; worldId, regionId, generator, and generatorVersion are omitted even though all are canonical GenerationOrigin fields.

Two records with the same WorldEntityId, kind, and recipeKey but different WorldId, RegionId, generator identity, or generator version therefore produce a diagnostic that cannot describe the provenance conflict that caused the duplicate.

Search of current open PR/issue titles and bodies for DuplicateIdentityDiagnostic/worldId found no active repair for this provenance-loss gap. Existing PR #276 hardens diagnostic immutability and ID boundaries, while the known registry-capacity and persistentState-budget findings are separate concerns.
This is source-only contract observability/debuggability work and claims no Studio, physics, networking, or Hero Gate evidence.
